chunks: Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Musa ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Mansour, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the shade for the one in Ihraam. He said: 'He should not shade except from a reason of illness.'

key_terms.عِلَّةِ مَرَضٍ: Reason of illness / excuse of sickness
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihraam (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muhrim to use shade during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the prohibition of using artificial shade (such as an umbrella or canopy) for the Muhrim is clarified as absolute unless necessitated by a specific 'illness' (illa), which Shia jurists interpret broadly to include extreme heat causing harm. This ruling distinguishes between the general prohibition of covering the head and the exception for medical or physical necessity, reflecting the principle of ease within the strictures of Ihraam. The hadith underscores the balance between ritual purity and physical well-being in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from Musa Bin Umar, from Muhammad Bin Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the shade for the one in Ihraam. Heasws said: ‘He should not shade except from a reason of illness’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad has narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Ushaym from Musa ibn ‘Umar from Muhammad ibn Mansur who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a man in the state of Ihram and shadows. He (the Imam) said, ’He must not seek shadows unless he is ill.’”
